turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, they told me I needed to come in, but honestly, I’m just here because I am at my wit's end trying to get someone, anyone, to actually look at the reality of my situation. Everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure on my house is just... just paperwork, you know? Like it's a simple matter of missed payments or a clerical thing, which is completely insulting. I'm a supervisor, I manage the whole floor at my retail job, I deal with inventory and schedules and numbers all day long, so I know when things don't add up. 

And I know, without a shadow of a doubt, that the bank, the loan servicer, and... and even people at my job, my own coworkers, have been quietly working together behind my back. It sounds impossible to people who haven't looked at the evidence, but they have been coordinating this whole elaborate thing to push me out of my house. It started small, just weird coincidences with my shifts changing right when I needed to make calls to the bank, or mail going missing, but now it's completely obvious. And they keep throwing these legal documents at me, these so-called official notices and ledgers, but no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing and experiencing for almost two years now. They think they can just bury me in paperwork and I won't notice the actual coordination happening right in front of me, but I see it. I've been seeing it since this whole nightmare started, and I just need someone to finally document what is actually going on instead of handing me another pamphlet about financial planning.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, unyielding belief that their bank, loan servicer, and coworkers are conspiring against them to take their house, and explicitly states that no contradictory evidence (official documents) will change their mind.

top_partial.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

turns.doctor_question: During this stressful time, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?
turns.patient_response:
Voices? Like... like imaginary voices? No. Absolutely not. I know exactly why you're asking that, by the way. People hear the word "coordination" or they hear about the bank working with my coworkers, and they immediately jump to, "Oh, she must be hearing things, she must be cracking under the stress of the foreclosure." But no, I don't hear phantom voices or weird sounds that aren't there. 

My hearing is perfectly fine, which is exactly the problem! I hear what is *actually* happening. Like... okay, for example, last Tuesday. I was just outside the breakroom near the inventory lockup, checking the overstock numbers for the floor, and I heard Sarah and Dave whispering. Real people, real voices. And they stopped dead, just completely silent, the absolute second I turned the corner. Or when I'm on the phone with the bank, I'll hear this distinct click—a real, physical click on the line—like someone else is picking up the extension to listen in. Probably someone from the servicer's office coordinating with my manager, making sure our stories don't line up. 

So I don't hear things that aren't there, doctor. I hear exactly what *is* there. I'm not sitting alone in my living room listening to the walls talk or hearing angels or whatever it is people do. I'm a professional, I have a degree, I know how to observe my surroundings. I am just dealing with real people having real conversations behind my back to ruin my life, and I just need someone to actually look at the facts of that instead of asking if I'm hallucinating.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that her coworkers and the bank are coordinating behind her back to ruin her life.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing imaginary voices, phantom sounds, or experiencing any auditory hallucinations.

turns.doctor_question: Before this situation with your home began two years ago, had you ever felt that other people or groups were working against you like this?
turns.patient_response:
No. No, definitely not. And that's... see, that's exactly why I know this is real, because I've never been the kind of person who thinks the world is out to get them. I mean, before two years ago? My life was completely normal. I've been at my job for six years, worked my way up to supervisor. I had good relationships with my coworkers. I mean, you know how retail is, there's always a little drama, someone complaining about the schedule or who has to work Black Friday, but it was just normal workplace stuff. I never thought anyone was actively trying to sabotage my life or take my house. 

I bought this house four years ago, and everything was fine. I made my payments, I kept up with the yard work, I even repainted the trim on the front porch myself. I had a whole routine. I'd go to work, deal with the vendors, manage the floor, come home, maybe watch some TV, pay my bills on time. I wasn't sitting around thinking my neighbors were spying on me or my boss was plotting my downfall. I was just living my life. 

It wasn't until the loan servicer changed—that was about two years ago, almost exactly—that things started getting weird. That's when the "lost" payments started, and the strange phone calls where they'd hang up if I asked too many questions. And then suddenly, right around the same time, Dave at work starts constantly asking me about my mortgage, like, "Hey, how's the house? Interest rates are crazy right now, huh?" Just probing, constantly. And then my shifts started getting changed without my approval, always on the days I had scheduled meetings with the bank's loss mitigation department. 

So no, doctor, I have never felt like this before. Because this has never happened to me before. I'm not paranoid, I'm just observant. I know the difference between normal life and... and whatever this coordinated attack is. If I was just a crazy person who thought everyone was out to get me, wouldn't I have felt this way my whole life? But I didn't. This started two years ago, specifically with these people, regarding this house. It's a targeted thing, not some lifelong delusion.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that there is a 'coordinated attack' involving their loan servicer and coworkers actively trying to sabotage their life and take their house.

turns.doctor_question: Around the time this started two years ago, did you experience any significant physical illnesses or medical issues?
turns.patient_response:
Medical issues? Like... like a brain tumor or something? No, no, nothing like that. I know why you're asking that, too. You're trying to find some biological reason, some... some medical excuse for why I'm seeing what I'm seeing. You're thinking, "Oh, maybe she had a stroke, maybe she has some sort of neurological condition that's making her paranoid." But I'm telling you, I am perfectly healthy. I mean, perfectly healthy. 

I haven't had so much as a bad flu in the last five years. I don't even get seasonal allergies. I take a multivitamin, I drink plenty of water, I try to get my steps in at work—which, believe me, you get plenty of steps in when you're managing a retail floor of that size, running back and forth from the registers to the stockroom. But as far as serious medical problems? Hospitalizations? Surgeries? No. None. Zero. 

The only thing I've dealt with, medically speaking, in the last two years is just the physical toll of the stress. You know, tension headaches from staring at spreadsheets and legal documents until two in the morning, trying to trace where my payments actually went. Maybe some acid reflux because I'm drinking too much coffee to stay awake so I can monitor my accounts, because God knows what they'll try to slip past me if I actually sleep for eight hours. And, you know, my back hurts sometimes, but that's just from standing on concrete floors all day, that's not... that's not some underlying disease. 

But a significant illness? Something that would cause, what, delirium? No. My brain is fine. My body is fine. The only thing that is sick here is the system that is allowing these people to collude against me, and the fact that no one will just look at the paper trail I've put together. I have binders, doctor. I have color-coded binders showing the discrepancies, the timeline of the shift changes, the phone records. If I was sick, if I was medically compromised, do you really think I'd be able to maintain that level of organization? I don't think so. So no, no medical issues. Just the stress of being the only person who sees the truth.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses fixed persecutory beliefs that people are colluding against her and trying to slip things past her, which she tracks with color-coded binders.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly denies having difficulty with organization, citing her ability to maintain color-coded binders and a high level of organization to track the perceived collusion.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever felt like an outside force was controlling your thoughts, body, or actions against your will?
turns.patient_response:
Controlling my thoughts? Like... like mind control? No, no, absolutely not. I mean, think about it, doctor. If they could control my thoughts or my actions, why would they go through all this trouble with the paperwork and the schedule changes? They would just... I don't know, make me sign the foreclosure papers and walk away, right? But they can't. Because I am one hundred percent in control of my own mind and my own body. Always have been. 

I make my own choices. When I sit down at night and cross-reference the servicer's timestamps with my work schedule, that is *me* doing that. My hands, my brain, my free will. No one is pulling my strings like some sort of puppet. Honestly, it's almost insulting that people might think that about me. I'm a supervisor! I manage a team of fifteen people on the sales floor. You don't get to do that, you don't get promoted to that level, if you can't even control your own actions. I decide when I walk down the aisle to check the endcaps, I decide when I call the bank to demand answers, I decide everything I do. 

The only thing they are controlling is the situation around me—the environment, the documents, the lies they tell each other. They're manipulating the system, not *me* physically. I know exactly what I'm thinking and why I'm thinking it. It's just... it's just so frustrating because every time I try to explain the actual, physical evidence of what they are doing to my mortgage, I get asked these... these sci-fi movie questions. No one is beaming thoughts into my head or making my arms move against my will. I'm just a normal woman trying to keep the house she bought, using her own perfectly functioning brain to fight back against a very real, very documented conspiracy. If someone else was controlling me, I wouldn't be fighting so hard, would I?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient explicitly describes a 'very real, very documented conspiracy' against her regarding her mortgage, confirming persecutory delusions, even though she denies delusions of control.
